raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Review UK motor position, competitive landscape, redress scheme, and Investment Bank's RWA target and RoTE strategy.",
  "main_topics": [
    "UK motor position",
    "competitive landscape",
    "redress scheme",
    "Investment Bank's RWA target",
    "RoTE strategy"
  ],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "Thank you very much, Chris Hallam from Goldman Sachs. So I guess one simple question, just to begin with, on UK motor, perhaps you could remind us, last quarter you provided some context and overview of your position in that segment, just a recap of that and also how you see the developments over the last 48 hours in terms of impact on the competitive landscape in the UK and also maybe with the potential redress scheme, the sort of growth focus from the UK government. And then secondly, separately, the Investment Bank, you have the 50% of group RWAs target. You have said repeatedly RoTE is the North Star. I think on the call, Jason's question about if the revenue number gets up that would support a higher RoTE outcome for the group. Is that the right way to think about it? That the 50% RWA target would be the one that sort of, you'd be happy to give in order to let the IB do what it can do and probably support outperformance versus targets?",
  "answer_quote": "Let me start with UK motor. So just to remind you, we exited the business and sold our business in its entirety in 2019. And up to that point, we'd had a low single digit market share. We were not a big participant in the market. We welcome the clarity and the reduction in uncertainty that's come from the Supreme Court ruling on Friday. And we also welcome the news from the FCA yesterday that they will consult on an industry wide redress scheme. So, we'll be spending time with them and the government ensuring that that is fair and balanced. And that's probably all I can say at this point, you know, given that we've yet to hear from the FCA in detail and, you know, this is live, coming out, but that's broadly where we are. So, nothing really to sort of add from where we've been in the past. On the second point, the 50% is, I would say, both an intent and an output. By an intent, what I mean is it's in service of growing a business with high returns and more stable returns. And that is the simple objective of the plan that we set out. And it's also an output, and it's an output from two really important, if you like, strategic plans within the plan itself. The first is our belief that we have the right waterfront and the right level of capital within the IB. And I think that we've shown that we can grow it and grow its returns within the waterfront that we've given it. And we did say at the outset that we felt there were areas where capital could become more efficient, and we still continue to see that. The second part of the jigsaw, which is less within our control, is clearly the growth in the UK to which we are committed both for the £30 billion [RWA growth] and beyond. You know, we're going to continue to want to grow those high returning businesses. The third piece of the jigsaw, which is less within our control, is clearly the timing of regulatory change. And that's clearly a factor in getting to that 50%. So, the timing of the implementation of the US card model could be 2026/2027 and somewhat out of our hands, Chris. But I think the really important part and the intent is maintaining capital in the IB, certain that we can grow within that and, and continuing to grow the UK group.",
  "reason": "The answer provides a complete response to the question, directly addressing the UK motor position, competitive landscape, redress scheme, and the Investment Bank's RWA target and RoTE strategy, with high evidence level and numeric evidence present."
}
